_comment: The only per-library configuration. Everything that changes the produced bytes is declared
here, so `build.py` can recompute the acquisition cache key without running anything and a
manifest edit is a cache miss rather than a stale read.
`environment.resolved` is this file's lockfile, and it exists for the same reason delta-rs
needed `lock_deps`: the declared pins are not a pin. `fastmcp==4.0.3` is a metapackage that
ships no code at all; it requires `fastmcp-slim[client,server]==4.0.3`, which in turn
requires `mcp>=2.0.0,<3.0.0` -- a RANGE. Two builds a month apart would see different
`AuthProvider` bases and a different `MCPError`. So acquisition resolves the graph, asserts
it matches `resolved` exactly, and aborts naming both sides if upstream moved.
Every extra is installed on purpose. Twelve fastmcp modules bind names under a module-level
`try: import X / except ImportError:` fallback, and Griffe records whichever branch is live.
Installing the full set is what makes the index describe the library as it actually runs
rather than as it degrades; `conditional.tsv` records the branch taken for each.

repository.name: fastmcp
repository.title: FastMCP capability repository
repository.description: The FastMCP server and client surface, the MCP wire types, and the official SDK, indexed at a pinned resolved environment.

tools.checker_note: The batch analysis producer. Pinned because the workstation carries a different release, and a capture from the wrong one describes a different tool while looking correct. Admitted by ADR-0046; ty remains the production engine.

environment.resolved_note: 101 distributions. Asserted against a fresh resolve; a mismatch aborts.

code_owner._why: `fastmcp`'s own RECORD is six lines of metadata. All 257 modules and every extra are owned by `fastmcp-slim`, so METADATA questions are answered against that distribution.

extras_documented.unlocks: A sampling handler that fulfils server sampling requests through Anthropic's API.
A sampling handler backed by the OpenAI API.
A sampling handler backed by google-genai, and the Gemini CLI install target.
FastMCPApp and the interactive app Providers -- approval, choice, form, file upload, generative UI.
The code-mode Transform, which exposes the tool catalog to a sandboxed interpreter instead of as individual tools.
Long-running task support; the fastmcp-tasks distribution.

environment.extras_note: Each row names modules rather than only prose, so verify.py can assert every named module is in the index. An extras table that drifts from the install line is worse than none: it tells a caller an optional dependency unlocks something it no longer unlocks.

distributions.namespace_note: `fastmcp/contrib/` has no `__init__.py`, so Griffe cannot reach it from the package root: `'contrib' in pkg.members` is False while `from fastmcp.contrib.mcp_mixin import MCPMixin` works. Its three subpackages are loaded explicitly, and anything still unreachable is written to not-indexed.tsv rather than silently dropped.

distributions.note: 462 classes in seven modules -- more than FastMCP itself. Defined in the private `_types`, re-exported through a 211-entry `__all__`, so the canonical path is one a caller must not write and the access path is the only usable spelling.
distributions.protocol_era_note: Era modules hold same-named copies of the same wire types because FastMCP negotiates a protocol era per connection. Never merge these on leaf name.

distributions.note: Indexed so the three-way `FastMCP` / `MCPServer` / tombstone distinction can be stated. `mcp/server/fastmcp.py` raises ModuleNotFoundError at import; the SDK's server class is `mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer`.

boundary._comment: Re-exported into an indexed __all__ but defined elsewhere. These become boundary rows in symbols.tsv -- findable by name, honestly marked as not indexed -- rather than vanishing. `Depends` is the dependency-injection entry point and lives in `uncalled_for`.

corpora.name: docs
corpora.note: The documentation site at the pinned tag. This is the half of the library that signatures cannot carry -- why you would choose a Provider over a Transform, what a deployment actually looks like. `python-sdk/` is excluded because it is a generated API reference and this repository already produces that from the installed code. `v2/` and `v3/` are excluded: the previous eras are a separate question from the current one, and removed-api.md already carries what 4.0 dropped.

corpora.name: examples
corpora.note: 125 .py + 30 .md at this tag. Feeds link.py, so an extension-point page can say which upstream example demonstrates it -- evidence from a structural match, not a name collision.

corpora.name: tests
corpora.note: 427 files. Where the auth, proxy and transform edge cases are actually demonstrated -- upstream's own executable statement of how a capability behaves.

corpora.name: spec-2026-07-28
corpora.note: The era `mcp_types._v2026_07_28` models. Pinned to a commit: this was declared against the `main` BRANCH, which is not a pin -- the determinism check would have broken the first time upstream pushed.

corpora.name: spec-2025-11-25
corpora.note: The era `mcp_types._v2025_11_25` models. Both ship because proxying across eras is a documented capability.
